_meta.title: Provisional Machiavellian ontology (Phase IV)
_meta.status: derived from pilot cases A-C plus Disc I.7/I.37/III.28 close reading; to be revised against full corpus
_meta.note: Variables marked discovered=true are Machiavelli's own analytic vocabulary, not imposed by the project brief's starting ontology.

variables.label: Humors (umori) — standing dispositional pressures of social groups
variables.notes: Machiavelli's master variable: class-specific desires (grandi: to command/acquire; popolo: not to be oppressed). Builds up like pressure; requires institutional venting.

variables.label: Orders (ordini) — institutional channels and constitutional arrangements
variables.notes: Presence/absence/quality of legally ordained channels (accuse, tribunate, dictatorship) is the key moderator between humors and outcomes.

variables.label: Legal accusation channels (accuse) before many judges
Ordinary vs extraordinary modes of political action
variables.notes: Binary classifier Machiavelli applies to every conflict resolution: within-ordini (safe) vs outside-ordini (ruinous).

variables.label: Reputation acquired through public ways (counsel, service)
Reputation acquired through private benefits (loans, dowries, protection, food)
variables.notes: Private largesse → partigiani → capacity to corrupt the public and force the laws.

variables.label: Partisan followings (partigiani, sette, parti)
Grain availability (public provision, imports, private stocks)
Discretionary control over food distribution
variables.notes: Withholding (Coriolanus) or granting (Maelius) food as political leverage; Machiavelli treats both as the same variable with opposite sign.

variables.label: Land ownership limits and distribution of conquered land
Public treasury rich / private citizens poor
Necessity vs ambition as motive regime
variables.notes: Once necessity is satisfied, ambition takes over; desire always exceeds capacity to acquire.

variables.label: Property (roba) vs honors (onori) as contested goods
variables.notes: Elites concede honors without extraordinary scandal but defend property obstinately.

variables.label: Tribunician power (creation, use, target of elite resentment)
Dictatorship as lawful emergency power
Senate as deliberative/price-setting/repressive body
Colony foundation as safety valve and strategic instrument
Recourse to external/foreign forces by internal factions
variables.notes: Diagnostic indicator: foreign intervention invited = proof of defective ordini.

variables.label: Elite temporizing repertoire (army out, tribune vs tribune, partial concession, colony)
Popular unrest (tumult, near-lynching, secession threat)
Institutional survival / republican liberty
Tyranny / regnum risk
Faction formation cascade (offense→fear→defense→partisans→parties→ruin)
Distance decay of popular demand for land
variables.notes: Remote conquered fields, hard to cultivate, are less desired — a geographic moderator Machiavelli adds to explain the law falling dormant.

variables.label: Timing/retroactivity of corrective legislation
variables.notes: Laws that look far backward against entrenched custom are scandalous; early correction of dangerous works is essential.
